message.content:
J.K. Rowling is best known for the **Harry Potter** series, but she has also written several other popular books (both under her own name and under the pseudonym Robert Galbraith). Here’s a quick rundown:

| Title | Year | Notes |
|-------|------|-------|
| **Harry Potter and the Philosopher’s Stone** (also *Sorcerer’s Stone* in the U.S.) | 1997 | First book in the Harry Potter series; introduces the wizarding world. |
| **Harry Potter and the Chamber of Secrets** | 1998 | Second book; expands on Hogwarts lore and introduces the Chamber. |
| **Harry Potter and the Prisoner of Azkaban** | 1999 | Third book; introduces Sirius Black and the Marauder’s Map. |
| **Harry Potter and the Goblet of Fire** | 2000 | Fourth book; features the Triwizard Tournament. |
| **Harry Potter and the Order of the Phoenix** | 2003 | Fifth book; focuses on the formation of Dumbledore’s Army. |
| **Harry Potter and the Half‑Blood Prince** | 2005 | Sixth book; delves into Voldemort’s past. |
| **Harry Potter and the Deathly Hallows** | 2007 | Seventh and final book; concludes the epic saga. |
| **Fantastic Beasts and Where to Find Them** | 2001 | Companion book to the Harry Potter films; later adapted into a film series. |
| **Quidditch Through the Ages** | 2001 | Another companion book detailing the history of Quidditch. |
| **The Tales of Beedle the Bard** | 2008 | A collection of wizarding fairy tales. |
| **The Casual Vacancy** | 2012 | Rowling’s first adult novel published under her own name; a dark political drama. |
| **The Cuckoo’s Calling** (as Robert Galbraith) | 2013 | First book in the Cormoran Strike detective series. |
| **The Silkworm** | 2014 | Second book in the Cormoran Strike series. |
| **Career of Evil** | 2015 | Third book in the Cormoran Strike series. |
| **Lethal White** | 2018 | Fourth book in the Cormoran Strike series. |
| **The Ickabog** | 2020 | A children’s fable published as a free e‑book during the COVID‑19 pandemic. |

These titles are among the most widely read and celebrated works by J.K. Rowling, spanning fantasy, mystery, and contemporary fiction.
